To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the leakage current of a register file cell can be greatly reduced by discharging the cell to '0' when the register is dead.
we propose a low-leachage register file cell for superscalar processors based on the observation of short life cycle of physical registers.

we propose a novel low-leakage design for register files that can reduce the leakage power of a 32-bit and a 64-bit datapath register file by 38% and by 47%, respectively, and can reduce the total energy consumption by 18%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
reducing leakage power in a superscalar register file, which is an important building block of modern microprocessor.
reducing the leakage power consumption of register files in high-end superscalar processors, which are one of the major sources of power consumption in the processor core.
the leakage power and energy reduction in the register file, a critical component in a superscalar microprocessor.

our design is the first low-leakage design that achieves both leakage and dynamic energy reduction.
the proposed design is an effective way to reduce leakage power in the register file.

our design is a very effective and low-cost solution to reduce leakage power for register files.

leakage reduction techniques can be developed without compromising performance.
